Actually reduction: Clique of size k in G corresponds to Vertex Cover of size |V|-k in complement graph? Wait classic: Clique in G corresponds to Vertex Cover in complement graph \bar{G}. Because a set of vertices forms a clique in G iff it forms an independent set in complement, and complement independent set of size k corresponds to vertex cover of size n - k (since complement of independent set is a vertex cover). So reduction: Input: n, edges of G, k. Output: n' = n, edges' = complement edges (i.e., all unordered pairs not in original edges and not self loops), k' = n - k.

k=1 always yes if n>=1. Then k' = n-1. Vertex cover of size <= n-1: For any graph with n vertices, is there always a vertex cover of size n-1? Yes, because you can take all vertices except one; that covers all edges because any edge incident to the missing vertex might be uncovered if edge exists between two other vertices? Wait if we exclude vertex v, edges between other vertices are covered because both endpoints are in the set. Edge incident to v: one endpoint is v (not in set) but the other endpoint is in set (since all other vertices are included). So all edges are covered. So yes, vertex cover of size n-1 always works. So matches.

k > n always no. Then k' = n - k < 0. Vertex cover with k' <0 is always no. Good.

Thus reduction works.

        require(0 <= u < n and 0 <= v < n, f"edge {edge!r} has a vertex outside 0..{n - 1}")

    require_int(num_vars, "num_vars", minimum=0)
    require(isinstance(clauses, list), "clauses must be a list")

        require(number >= 0, f"numbers must be >= 0, got {number}")

class Clique:
    """Clique.

    Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}

      * k is any integer.

    Edge cases: k <= 0 is always yes. k = 1 is yes whenever n >= 1. k > n is

    """

    name = 'Clique'

    @classmethod

        validate_graph_with_k(instance)
